title: Networks of Causal Abstractions: A Sheaf-theoretic Framework
authors: Gabriele D'Acunto, Paolo Di Lorenzo, Sergio Barbarossa
relevance: Source of the causal abstraction network and sheaf-consistency diffusion that our gate decides whether to run against each neighbor.

title: Toward a spectral theory of cellular sheaves
venue: Journal of Applied and Computational Topology 3, 315-358
relevance: Provides the sheaf Laplacian and harmonic-section theory underlying consensus of local causal models across the agent graph.

title: Abstracting Causal Models
relevance: Defines constructive causal abstraction; our edge maps between specialists' models are abstractions in this sense.

title: Information Value Theory
venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics 2(1), 22-26
relevance: Origin of expected value of information; our gate thresholds the VOI of a neighbor's causal evidence against alignment cost.

title: Principles of Metareasoning
relevance: Rational metareasoning: treat alignment computations as actions chosen by expected utility gain minus time cost.

title: Reasoning About Beliefs and Actions Under Computational Resource Constraints
relevance: Decision-theoretic control of inference under resource limits, which motivates gating rather than always fusing neighbors.

title: Act-Then-Measure: Reinforcement Learning for Partially Observable Environments with Active Measuring
authors: Merlijn Krale, Thiago D. Simao, Nils Jansen
relevance: Modern RL formulation where measuring is a costed action bounded by value of information; we gate evidence acquisition the same way.

title: Learning when to Communicate at Scale in Multiagent Cooperative and Competitive Tasks
authors: Amanpreet Singh, Tushar Jain, Sainbayar Sukhbaatar
relevance: IC3Net learns a binary communication gate per agent; we contrast its learned gate with an explicit VOI criterion.

title: Learning Attentional Communication for Multi-Agent Cooperation
relevance: ATOC's attention unit decides when to form communication groups; a learned precursor to our acquisition gate.

title: Learning Individually Inferred Communication for Multi-Agent Cooperation
authors: Ziluo Ding, Tiejun Huang, Zongqing Lu
relevance: I2C infers one-to-one communication need via causal effect of a neighbor on one's policy, closest in spirit to our gate.

title: Context-Aware Sparse Deep Coordination Graphs
authors: Tonghan Wang, Liang Zeng, Weijun Dong, Qianlan Yang, Yang Yu, Chongjie Zhang
relevance: Sparsifies coordination graphs by a variance-of-payoff criterion; we sparsify alignment edges by VOI instead.

title: Causal Policy Gradient for Whole-Body Mobile Manipulation
authors: Jiaheng Hu, Peter Stone, Roberto Martin-Martin
relevance: Causal MoMa discovers action-to-reward causal dependencies for whole-body control; our specialists carry such local causal models.

title: Defining and Characterizing Reward Gaming
authors: Joar Skalse, Nikolaus H. R. Howe, Dmitrii Krasheninnikov, David Krueger
relevance: Formalizes proxy-reward hacking; motivates our process verifier as a guard against optimizing a hackable alignment proxy.

title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Shielding
authors: Mohammed Alshiekh, Roderick Bloem, Rudiger Ehlers, Bettina Konighofer, Scott Niekum, Ufuk Topcu
relevance: Shield that overrides unsafe actions against a temporal-logic spec; our force-limit and cabinet-motion verifier plays this role.

title: A non-divergent estimation algorithm in the presence of unknown correlations
authors: Simon J. Julier, Jeffrey K. Uhlmann
relevance: Covariance intersection fuses Gaussian beliefs with unknown shared information, avoiding double-counting a common prior.
